fragments.text: Good day, everyone. My name is Sandra E. Maynard. I am the Pro Vice-Chancellor of Global Affairs at the University of the West Indies and the President of the International School for Development Justice. It's my pleasure to speak here today around AI governance, a Caribbean regional imperative. Now, when we consider Caribbean AI governance, it is essential, not optional. When we consider that AI is reshaping the world economies through automation, data, analytics and intelligence system that enhance productivity across sectors. For the Caribbean, this transformation occurs within a unique context of being small island developing states with limited resources, high connectivity costs and economies heavily dependent on tourism, agriculture and services. Now, this is not to the exclusion of other small island developing states but the Caribbean region faces a real digital divide paradox.
fragments.summary: I am the Pro Vice-Chancellor of Global Affairs at the University of the West Indies and the President of the International School for Development Justice.
